jobs.description:
The Business Analyst – Investment Governance & Performance plays a pivotal role in shaping our global retail footprint. In this role you will be responsible for optimizing and controlling all Pandora’s investments in store leases, acquisitions and other network actions. By owning and driving best practices in investment evaluation, you will help support the strategic growth and profitability through data-driven decision-making on our global store network.

You will work closely with the Franchise & Network Management Team as well as local property and network teams, delivering high-quality analysis and recommendations to drive strategic initiatives such as store openings, closures, relocations, Forward Integrations and lease renewals.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• 
Evaluate and Review Investment Proposals.

• 
Ensure the accuracy and completeness of all submitted investment proposals (IPs).

• 
Validate compliance with accounting standards, including IFRS16 regulations.

• 
Assess business cases for financial impact and strategic alignment.

• 
Share approved IPs with the CCO/CEO/CFO for final sign-off.

• 
Track, Report and Analyse Investments.

• 
Maintain and update the global investment overview.

• 
Report and review the investment proposals vs actual performance in the hindsight report to measure accuracy.

• 
Deliver insights to enhance the accuracy of future investment decisions.

• 
Lead Bi-Weekly Investment Review Meetings

• 
Coordinate and host approval meetings with the Global Network & Franchise management team.

• 
Present investment proposals from market clusters for review and global approval.

• 
Develop and Improve Internal Tools and Processes

• 
Continuously improve reports, presentations and templates to reflect the strategic priorities and regulatory requirements.

• 
Promote and implement global best practices across clusters.

• 
Cross-Functional Collaboration

• 
Act as a trusted advisor to Global Network & Franchise management, Global Finance, Cluster Property and Cluster finance teams.

• 
Provide analytical support and challenge local teams to ensure business cases are both realistic and profitable.

**Your team

**The Global Network Development & Insights function partners with the Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) organization to provide strategic insights that shape Pandora’s global retail and franchise network. The team collaborates closely with Cluster Finance Directors and General Managers to drive performance, ensure retail excellence, and execute on global priorities.

You will report to the Network Expansion & Investments Senior Manager and join a high-impact team focused on data-led strategy and investment optimization.

**What We’re Looking For

**We are looking for a proactive and analytical team player with a strong business acumen and a critical mindset. You have a talent for transforming data into insights and a passion for driving performance through collaboration and strategic thinking.

**Your Qualifications Include

**

• A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.

• Minimum 2 years of experience in a similar role; experience in retail, real estate, fashion or FMCG is a plus.

• Proven ability to deliver insights through reports, dashboards, and presentations.

• Strong stakeholder management skills, including experience communicating with senior leadership.

• Proficiency in MS Excel; experience with Power Automate and Power BI/Query is a strong advantage.

**AI & Automation/Optimization

**We expect our future colleague to actively embrace the evolving role of AI and automation in business analysis. This means leveraging AI-powered tools to streamline investment evaluation workflows and enhance reporting accuracy.

**Additional Information

**Global Career Band: 5B

Start date: Ideally, January 1, 2027

**Did we get your attention?

**We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you would like to become part of Pandora's future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site at Pandora Group.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable **and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.****About Pandora

**Pandora is the world’s largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores. Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: The Department of Organization (IOA) is looking for a student assistant for a qualitative research program on the impact of large-scale funding on recipient organizations
jobs.description:
We are looking for a student assistant who will be a member of the GRANDER research team and support key research tasks related to data management, analysis, and giving practical support to the research team.

GRANDER is a research program at the Department of Organization, Copenhagen Business School, studying the impact of large-scale philanthropic funding on organizations and their outcomes. The program is led by Associate Professor Jane Bjørn Vedel and runs until 2032.

We do ambitious research in an inspiring setup on an important societal topic, based on large qualitative data sets collected over many years.

The position offers first-hand insight into qualitative research at the highest level – a strong foundation for your further studies and your master’s thesis.

Tasks in the position

• Organizing our data and preparing raw data for analysis – e.g., receiving interviews and documents, transcribing, logging and archiving data

• Collecting archival data and background information

• Analyzing data – e.g., coding data in NVivo and Excel; creating evidence tables; developing timelines and models based on data

• Supporting literature reviews – e.g., performing Scopus searches, downloading and filing articles, and coding articles

• Supporting events and meetings, and other practical tasks

The position is 12 hours per week, mainly at CBS Kilen, and some flexibility in scheduling is required.

Requirements for experience/qualifications and personal skills

We value the following qualifications – you are:

• thorough, systematic and detail-oriented

• analytically strong, interested in both data and theory, and open to learning new methods

• team-oriented, helpful and flexible when needed

• able to handle confidential material with great care

• highly proficient in English, written and spoken

• enrolled in a relevant degree program in the social sciences

We offer a position in an inspiring research environment characterized by high ambition, passion for research and a willingness to go far to do excellent and impactful work. You will work closely with the project leader and the team, gain insight into how a large qualitative research project is run – from data collection to publication – and learn a lot along the way.

Salary and terms of employment

Employment takes place in accordance with the HK organisational agreement and the Collective Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and Publicly Employed Organisations (OAO-S Collective Agreement).

The salary currently ranges between DKK 145.73 and DKK 152.88 per hour and is dependent on previous employment in the office profession and level of education. The pension contribution amounts to 16% of the pensionable salary components.

It is a prerequisite for employment that you are an active student at a higher educational institution.

The employment is time-limited for the period from January 15, 2027, to June 30, 2028.

The recruitment process

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. A recruitment committee will assess applications and call a selection of qualified candidates for an interview.

One of CBS' strategic goals is to promote diversity and inclusion in our organisation. Therefore, we strive for a hiring process that reduces potential bias. Consequently, we encourage applicants not to include photos or unnecessary information about personal circumstances in the application.

Additional information

If you want to know more about the job content, please contact Associate Professor Jane Bjørn Vedel, email: jbv.ioa@cbs.dk.

Your application

You apply for the position online, where you fill in the application form and attach your application with information about previous employment, exam papers and CV.

Interviews are expected to be held in the first half of December.

WE TRANSFORM SOCIETY WITH BUSINESS

Copenhagen Business School (CBS) is an international university focused on the opportunities and challenges facing the business community and society. Through research, education and collaboration with the world around us, we work to drive positive change in society.

Our strategy, We transform society with business, guides everything we do. At CBS, researchers, lecturers and administrative employees bring different competences to the table, working together towards a shared ambition.

CBS is located in Frederiksberg, close to the centre of Copenhagen. Our campus is home to an international community of students, researchers and employees and is also open to the wider community.

CBS is working continuously on becoming a diverse and inclusive organisation, and we encourage all regardless of gender identity and expression, ethnicity, religious beliefs, LGBT+ status, cultural background etc. to apply. Reach out to us if you need assistance in the application or recruitment process, if there is something we should know, or if as a person with disability you wish to make use of your preferential access.

We transform society with business.

The Interacting Minds Center, Department of Culture and Society is looking for a student assistant (HK) to work on a research project related to parenting and paternity leave. The project is funded by the Carlsberg Foundation: http://bit.ly/Carlsberg_project. The position will be supervised by Christine Parsons.

The period of employment is 20st Jan 2027 until 31st Dec 2027.

The student assistant will assist with participant recruitment, data management and data analysis and contribute to dissemination of research.

Tasks:

• analysing data, visualizing results

Qualifications:

Salary and other conditions of employment are in accordance with the applicable collective agreement. The position is for an average of 6 hours per week, but the workload may vary.

Please write a short motivation and attach your CV.

Questions about the position can be directed to Christine Parsons (Christine.parsons@cas.au.dk)

Salary and terms of employment

You will be employed under the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Organisations of Public Employees – Denmark (OAO-S Collective Agreement, State Sector), as well as the organisational agreement for clerical employees, laboratory technicians and IT staff (HK).

You will be placed as a clerical employee in pay group 2–3, depending on education and qualifications.

**Your impact begins here

**As Safety Surveillance Principal Specialist, you will be the safety lead for several products in Novo’s early pipeline, working where non-clinical and clinical development meet. You will turn emerging data into a clear early safety profile and shape decisions for first-in-human and early clinical studies. Your scientific judgement will help protect the people taking part in these studies and give development teams the clarity to move at pace.

**What You’ll Bring

**You are a scientist first. You are confident, outgoing and driven, and you want to be in the room where early safety decisions are made.

• A PhD, MD, DVM, MSc Pharm or equivalent in Medicine or Natural Sciences, with extensive experience in pharmacovigilance or early-phase pharmaceutical development.

• A solid understanding of drug development processes, global regulatory requirements and GxP standards.

• A strong grasp of medical concepts, disease mechanisms and scientific methodology. You use data to build scientific understanding, rather than letting the data lead you.

• The ability to identify challenges, shape strategies and turn them into clear, actionable steps.

• Confidence to take informed scientific risks and make a call, while never compromising on patient safety.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to guide and influence others through mentorship and informal leadership.

• A self-driven, ethical and adaptable approach. You work independently, address issues proactively and stay flexible when priorities change.

**What You’ll Do

**

• Own the early safety profile of products, evaluating emerging pre-clinical and clinical safety data to guide patient surveillance and business decisions.

• Lead the resolution of complex safety challenges and provide strong scientific and medical input across development activities.

• Shape study designs, clinical protocols and benefit-risk assessments, working to ambitious development timelines.

• Chair a cross-functional drug safety committee and represent Safety Surveillance in key cross-functional teams.

• Drive initiatives that strengthen scientific, strategic and operational excellence within Safety Surveillance.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Safety Surveillance Early Development, part of Global Patient Safety in Research & Development. It is a team of 8 colleagues in Denmark, and it handles all First Human Dose (FHD) studies across all indications at Novo. The team provides scientific safety expertise to early-stage projects, contributes to safety strategy and supports protocol review, risk assessments, early signal detection and cross-functional safety forums.

Your closest partners will be the non-clinical project manager, the medical specialist and the clinical pharmacologist. Together you will design studies that are scientifically strong and move quickly. You will also work with skilled colleagues across Non-clinical and Clinical Development, and across several therapeutic areas.

The environment is dynamic, collaborative and highly engaged. Colleagues share scientific insights, speak openly and support one another when evaluating complex safety data. Everyone is focused on doing what is best for the people we serve.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will have real ownership. As safety lead, you will be trusted to work independently, make your voice heard and influence decisions that guide early development. You will keep learning from colleagues across Non-clinical and Clinical Development, and you will help strengthen a culture of knowledge sharing and openness in the team.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000 to

1,245,100 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

The Data Platform IT team at Danske Bank is looking for a Cloud Platform Engineer to design, build, and continuously improve the Databricks platform that underpins data capabilities across the organization. Your work will shape the reliability and scalability of a platform used by engineers, architects, and data practitioners every day. In return, you will grow your skills in a collaborative environment with real technical depth.

What you will be doing

You will join a team of engineers and architects working on a platform that matters. The Data Platform IT squad operates with a high degree of technical ownership, and you will work closely with platform users, architects, and fellow engineers to translate real needs into self-service capabilities. The team values pragmatic thinking, open collaboration, and continuous improvement, and you will contribute to shaping how the platform evolves across environments.

In your day-to-day work, you will:

• 
Design and build scalable capabilities on the Databricks platform across environments

• 
Develop automation using Infrastructure as Code, primarily Terraform

• 
Improve CI/CD and release automation using GitHub Enterprise Cloud and related tooling

• 
Build observability, monitoring, alerting, and automated remediation across the platform

• 
Implement security, identity and access management, and data governance capabilities

• 
Troubleshoot complex platform issues and contribute to stable production operations

• 
Collaborate with engineers, architects, and platform users to deliver self-service solutions

About you

• 
Solid experience in cloud platform engineering, preferably on AWS

• 
Experience with Databricks or a comparable enterprise data platform

• 
Skilled with Infrastructure as Code tools, preferably Terraform

• 
Familiarity with CI/CD, version control, and software engineering practices including GitHub or Azure DevOps

• 
Experience with identity and access management, platform security, and governance controls

• 
Understanding of monitoring, logging, observability, and production platform operations at scale

• 
Clear communicator who collaborates across disciplines and takes pragmatic technical ownership

If you have experience in adjacent areas of cloud or data platform engineering, we welcome your application even if your background does not match every point above.

What we offer you

You will be part of a team where your technical contributions make a tangible difference to the data capabilities of a major financial institution. We support hybrid working, with three to four days per week in the office to encourage collaboration and knowledge sharing. You will have access to learning opportunities and the chance to develop your expertise alongside skilled colleagues.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, please get in touch with hiring manager Vladimiras Cincikas at vlci@danskebank.lt with any questions, or apply directly through our careers page.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by the 27th of November, 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Join us in this role where you’ll own and continuously develop our fundamental view of European power markets. Working at the intersection of market analysis and trading, you’ll bring together insights from across the organisation, form an independent view of where markets are heading, and translate this into clear commercial recommendations.

Working closely with the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, and traders, you’ll influence decisions around trading strategies, hedging, portfolio management, and PPAs. Rather than supporting decisions from a distance, you’ll be a trusted market expert whose analysis and judgement help shape the positions we take.

**Welcome to Trading & Revenue

**You’ll be part of Forecasting & Analysis where you, together with your colleagues, will provide the market insights and analysis behind key trading and commercial decisions.   You’ll work in a dynamic environment close to the trade floor, collaborating with traders, analysts, meteorologists, and dedicated in-house model developers. With strong modelling capabilities around you, you’ll be able to focus on interpreting what is happening in the market, challenging existing assumptions, forming a strong fundamental view, and translating it into commercial opportunities.

As a team, we challenge our thinking, share our expertise openly, and combine different perspectives to make better decisions.

In this role, your analysis becomes action. You’ll engage directly with Trading & Revenue senior leadership team and have the opportunity to shape how we understand European power markets. You’ll play a leading role in strengthening our market analysis capability, bringing in external perspectives and best practices, and developing a more integrated view across Trading & Revenue.

You’ll play an important role in:

• owning, developing, and maintaining our fundamental view of European power markets, with a particular focus on North-Western Europe and the UK, and bringing together perspectives from across Trading & Revenue into a coherent market outlook

• acting as a trusted sparring partner to the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, traders, and portfolio managers, bringing an independent fundamental market perspective to key strategic and commercial decisions

• identifying structural and emerging shifts across supply, demand, regulation, weather, generation, interconnector flows, electrification, and other market drivers, and assessing what they mean for power prices and market dynamics

• turning market developments into commercial implications, from understanding the impact of changing generation availability or demand assumptions to assessing what these developments mean for our portfolios and trading positions

• translating fundamental market insights into actionable trading and hedging strategies together with our trading teams, helping facilitate discussions on what positions we should take as market conditions and assumptions evolve

• advising senior stakeholders on the market implications of important portfolio, PPA, and other commercial decisions, bringing a clear view of both market opportunities and risks

• advancing our fundamental power market capability by bringing together perspectives from across the organisation, introducing external insights and industry best practices, and strengthening how we form and communicate our market view across Trading & Revenue.

To succeed in the role, you:

• have deep expertise in European power markets and significant experience forming an independent view of how fundamental developments affect power prices and market dynamics

• bring strong commercial judgement and can move confidently from fundamental analysis to clear recommendations on trading, hedging, portfolio, and PPA decisions

• understand the interaction between physical power market fundamentals, forward markets, options, and curve dynamics, and can connect changes in the physical market with their commercial and trading implications

• are comfortable owning a market view, challenging established assumptions, and acting as an equal sparring partner to experienced traders and senior decision-makers

• can look beyond established market assumptions, identify developments or structural shifts that may not yet be fully reflected in the market view, and determine what they could mean for future power prices

• can bring together different sources of analysis, modelling, external intelligence, and perspectives from across the organisation to form a clear and coherent market view

• communicate complex market developments as concise, decisive, and commercially relevant recommendations, including to senior stakeholders

• bring substantial experience from power or closely related European energy markets, whether gained in a utility, trading environment, financial institution, or similar market-facing organization.

jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Global Clinical Drug Supply
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

Genmab is seeking an experienced (Senior) Clinical Drug Supply Manager to join Global Clinical Drug Supply (GCDS) Manufacturing in Copenhagen.

The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality clinical trial supplies for both early and late-stage trials. In addition, this position offers significant influence over the refinement of Genmab’s processes, both within the GCDS Manufacturing function and cross-functionally to ensure scalability.

The (Senior) Clinical Drug Supply Manager will resolve complex operational challenges, lead strategic initiatives and mentor colleagues. A key focus of this role will be supporting team members through troubleshooting, problem-solving, and developing mitigation plans for complex issues related to packaging and labelling activities. This role requires balancing urgency and importance in a dynamic environment while serving as a positive role model for the team, by bringing a strong can-do attitude to drive solutions and inspire others.

The position reports to the Associate Director, Team Lead, Global Clinical Drug Supply Manufacturing based in Princeton.

**Responsibilities

**Responsibilities will be adjusted based on level of experience, and may include the following:

• Manage operational trial and project objectives related to packaging and labelling, providing proactive oversight to meet goals.

• Oversee inspection readiness and ensure compliance with relevant GMP, GDP and GCP regulations.

• Engage with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment and successful collaboration.

• Supervise and monitor vendor performance, ensuring delivery aligns with timelines and SOW.

• Provide direct support to team members in troubleshooting and problem resolution, ensuring effective development of mitigation plans for operational challenges.

• Mentor and coach team members, fostering a collaborative and high-performing environment.

• Lead complex GCDS Manufacturing projects within the area of clinical drug supply management.

• Develop, maintain and implement SOPs for drug supply processes and manage cross-functional collaborations.

**Qualifications

**

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant area (e.g., pharma, science, engineering, or supply chain management).

• Minimum 3 years of experience at manager level, and minimum 6+ years’ experience for Senior Manager. Ideally demonstrated skills with global CMO vendor collaboration and oversight of clinical packaging and labelling activities.

• Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional projects with an innovative and entrepreneurial mindset.

• Collaborative, proactive, and goal-oriented team player who inspires colleagues while fostering strong relationships.

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

• Extensive knowledge of GMP, GDP, and GCP regulations.

• Excellent communication skills in English, both oral and written.

**The Team

**You will join a highly competent team focused on packaging and labelling clinical trial supplies, collaborating closely with the Global Clinical Drug Supply Execution team. Together with the Global Clinical Drug Supply Systems team and Global Clinical Drug Supply Strategy team, these four functions form the Global Clinical Drug Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

**Application

**If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to upload your CV and cover letter outlining your motivation for the position. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews will be scheduled accordingly. Please note, fully remote applicants will not be considered; candidates must be within commuting distance of Copenhagen.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK687.888,00---1.031.832,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

**In this Director of Legal role, you’ll be…

**

• Serving as the legal partner to Sales by driving commercial SaaS contracting, handling T&Cs, MSAs, and DPAs, negotiating deviations, and maintaining fallback negotiation playbooks.

• Managing corporate legal matters, including entity management across international markets, governance, board support, and selective coordination with external counsel.

• Supporting the company's compliance framework in close partnership with our existing Compliance function, with a path toward taking over internal compliance ownership in the near future.

• Owning vendor and supplier contracting by reviewing and negotiating key terms on liability, security, privacy, and SLAs alongside Finance and Operations.

• Building and scaling a lean legal operating model by proactively driving processes, internal guidance, and review triggers to keep legal operations efficient.

• Supporting fundraising rounds, corporate structuring, and M&A initiatives in close collaboration with the CFO and leadership team.

**Who is the Legal Team?

**Sitting within Finance & Operations, the Legal function drives our overall legal direction while remaining hands-on in building a scalable framework that supports our rapid growth across European markets. We safeguard the company across commercial SaaS contracting, corporate law, international scaling, and vendor management, while supporting future fundraising and M&A activities.

We act as a close partner to executive stakeholders, Sales, Finance, and Security, balancing fast risk-reward decisions with robust corporate governance. You will work directly with the Chief Financial Officer and lead our Corporate Lawyer in an environment that values extreme ownership, pragmatic decision-making, and strong cross-functional collaboration to enable business velocity.

Essentially, we contribute to our vision by protecting the business and providing the legal backbone needed to scale our platform across international markets safely and efficiently.

**What you’ll bring:

**

• Ideally, +5-10 years of relevant legal experience in a similar role, with proven exposure to a fast-growing SaaS environment that has scaled internationally.

• A hands-on, autonomous mindset with the drive to take full ownership of the legal function and scale it from the current setup.

• Strong expertise in commercial SaaS contracting and negotiating client-facing terms.

• GDPR and data privacy expertise, with experience maintaining compliance frameworks.

• Experience with corporate law and governance (board and shareholder matters, entity management), plus exposure to fundraising and M&A processes alongside external counsel.

• A pragmatic, business-oriented mindset with a strong grasp of risk-reward balance to keep sales velocity high while protecting the business.

• Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with fluency in English (Danish is not a requirement).

**What do we offer you?

**

• A starting salary of 115,000 DKK per month. As you grow within this role, your compensation can grow with you up to 130,000 DKK per month.

• Continuous development through a clear and transparent framework, so you always know what the next step looks like through bi-annual growth talks and regular check-ins.

• Thorough pre- and onboarding to set you up for success.

• An office-first culture in a centrally located office near Kødbyen, along with visa and relocation support if needed.

• A culture of ownership, trust, and independence with the support you need.

• A strong team spirit where we celebrate wins and enjoy time together across offices.

• Our annual Global Summit, where the whole company meets and connects.

**Our recruitment process

**

• 30-minute online interview with our Talent Acquisition Partner

• 30-minute online interview with our CFO

• Completion of Personality Assessment & Case Presentation

• 60-minute in-person final case interview with our CFO & other relevant stakeholders

• Cultural interview with relevant stakeholders across the organisation

**About Formalize

**Formalize is a tech company founded in 2021 with offices in Aarhus, Copenhagen, Milan, Madrid, Munich & Paris. Currently, we are a team of +200 people from +30 nationalities operating in multiple European markets and are one of the fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups. We thrive on ambition, deliver impact through pragmatism, and embrace passion and honesty. We celebrate our wins, learn from our mistakes, and grow together as a team.

Our journey began within the whistleblowing compliance sector, highlighted by the award-winning Whistleblower Software by Formalize, laying the foundation for our success story. Now, we have extended our expertise to a larger compliance universe, including data compliance, risk, and privacy. Our Formalize product helps companies to effortlessly navigate and stay ahead in the ever-changing landscape of compliance. Our platform adapts to regulatory changes, continuously adapting to meet and foresee the evolving needs of our users, ensuring businesses remain compliant and confident in their operations.

Still curious? Read more about us here: About Formalize.

****Ready to apply?

****We will hold interviews and hire on an ongoing basis. For more information or questions, please contact the responsible recruiter in the Talent Acquisition team. Apply now with your resume and other relevant information through our Career Page. We look forward to seeing your application!

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

If so, we are looking for dedicated, curious, and highly motivated graduates to join the DFDS Graduate Programme starting in September 2027.

Be part of the movement - and play your part.  **About The Finance Graduate Programme

**The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry. With several acquisitions and continued growth across Europe, our Finance Division plays a key role in supporting business performance, driving strategic decision-making, and enabling sustainable growth across DFDS.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Finance Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters (HQ) will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the business partnering and HQ functions of our Finance Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

**Finance at DFDS

**Finance is at the heart of supporting our business and helping DFDS make informed decisions across our shipping and logistics operations.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be

**

• Support business performance analysis and partner with stakeholders across functions and markets.

• Contribute to forecasting and planning processes, helping identify opportunities and areas requiring further analysis.

• Work with financial reporting, consolidation, accounting, and performance management.

• Develop KPI reporting and management insights to support business decisions.

• Deliver analyses and recommendations to management, highlighting performance trends, risks, and opportunities.

• Gain exposure to strategic projects, investments, and initiatives supporting the continued growth of DFDS.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and collaborate with teams across our business units, group functions, and senior leadership. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

**About You

**At DFDS, we believe the strongest teams are built on diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have graduated from a relevant master’s degree by the start of the Graduate Programme in September 2027.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

Working at DFDS **Join the movement and grow with us.

**As part of the DFDS Graduate Programme, you will become part of a strong graduate network across the company and build valuable connections across our international business. We offer a steep learning curve, meaningful responsibility from day one, and three interesting rotations designed to accelerate your professional development.

Are we a match? Apply now.  If your skills, experience, aspirations, and personality match this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Please Apply By Uploading Your CV No Later Than 30 November 2026. When Applying, You’re Also Asked To Answer The Following Questions

• Why are you interested in joining the DFDS Graduate Programme?

• How will the programme help kickstart your career?

• How do you expect to contribute to the programme and DFDS?

• What do you believe will be your biggest challenge(s) during the programme?

**We look forward to hearing from you.

**Visit our Graduate site here to learn more and meet some of our people.

jobs.occupation: Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management
jobs.description:
Drive meaningful impact across the life sciences industry.

As our next Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups -locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most.

About the role

As a Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will work closely with clients and colleagues to address complex challenges across the life sciences value chain. You will take ownership of your work and contribute to delivering solutions that create real, lasting impact. This is a Senior role designed to provide project and program leadership to deliver strategic technical solutions that address complex client issues in the Life Sciences industry. You will be handling implementation/migration projects and programs to achieve desired outcomes and ensure successful business growth. You will also seek new business opportunities to help BASE life science grow its presence within existing and new customers.

Additionally, you will contribute to internal initiatives and training to further strengthen BASE life science’s project and program management methodologies, approach, and tools.

You will lead teams consisting of multiple workstreams, which could include BASE/Infosys, external third party, or client stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in, project/program management and the ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing responses to Requests for Proposals (RfPs), ensuring adequate planning for scope, timelines and budget

• Monitoring project/program status including milestones, risks, issues, budgets, etc.

• Acting as a delivery escalation point and proactively ensuring escalations are handled promptly with a clear action and communication plan.

• Creating and delivering tailored communication based on audience, i.e., executive level summaries for client stakeholders, or senior executives in BASE life science, status reports at a project or program-level at a suitable cadence for team members

• Intervening, when necessary, to ensure costs, timelines and quality are on track.

• Lead a cross-functional team to deliver projects/programs to the required scope, on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our life science industry stakeholders.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders in the life science industry to understand their needs and translate them into executable plans for the project team.

• Develop plans, timelines, and budgets for projects/programs for which you are responsible.

• Track and report on project/program progress, identifying and mitigating risks as needed.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration between the project team, life science industry stakeholders, and other teams within BASE life science.

You bring:

• 5+ years of experience as a technical project/program manager within Regulatory, Clinical, Quality or other GxP areas in the life science industry.

• Successful track record of managing technically complex projects/programs such as software development, implementation of IT systems, data migrations, etc.

• Experience leading technical teams and delivering data driven projects/programs.

• Experience with project management tools such as JIRA, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project etc.

• Experience with Agile project management methodologies such as SAFe.

• Strong communication skills, both in writing, meetings and in presentations.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.

Additionally, the ideal candidate has the following skills/certifications:

• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

• Experience selling either projects or products to clients.

• Experience working with Veeva Vault, SalesForce or similar technologies.

• Experience working with AI professionally

This position is offered in Denmark and Spain.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2015, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting company working exclusively in life sciences, built on a simple purpose: grow our people, and deliver real impact for our customers.

We don't think AI is a feature you bolt onto existing systems — we think it's the layer through which a life sciences company's strategy actually gets executed, end to end. Most of the industry is still proving AI can do one task at a time, function by function, pilot by pilot. We're building toward something bigger: AI that runs across clinical, regulatory, quality, and commercial work instead of stopping at the edges of a single application.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Spain, Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and the US, we work with top-10 pharma and ambitious biotechs alike, and with technology partners including Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, and Amass — turning that belief into deployed, compliant, sellable solutions, not slideware.

Why join BASE Life Science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact — grounded in five core values: team spirit, trust, openness, ambition, and execution.

• Ambition, encouraged through ownership and continuous learning.

• Execution — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice.

• Openness — your ideas are heard, challenged constructively, and supported as you grow.

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance.

• The opportunity to shape a practice, not just staff one.

Alongside this, we offer:

• Support for health and wellbeing, covering physical, mental, and social needs

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• Ongoing learning and professional development throughout your career

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

• Recognition of performance and impact, linked to contribution and results

• The opportunity to work on challenges that make a meaningful difference for patients and healthcare systems worldwide

Explore our work, values, and people at www.baselifescience.com

Interested?

If you find this position intriguing, don't delay—submit your application in English at your earliest convenience. We are continuously reviewing and assessing all incoming candidates and eagerly await your application.

At BASE Life Science, we value diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Employment decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs

Strategy meets execution and collaboration

In this role, you will support the successful delivery of high-impact projects and strategic workstreams that require close cross-functional collaboration. You’ll work alongside the Senior Manager to define and execute SC&D’s strategic priorities, ensuring best-in-class project management practices across the organization. • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics

Your new team

From our Copenhagen HQ, we collaborate across functions and markets to bring Pandora’s vision to life.

Additional information

Global career band: 5A

Did we get your attention?

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting, and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion in 2025.
